Kaikuvaara Oy
Regarding: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

I saw the Senior Signal Processing Engineer opening at Kaikuvaara and wanted to write. I have been following the Oulu RF and photonics engineering community for a few years now, initially through conference papers and more recently through colleagues who have worked with companies in the region. For a city its size, the concentration of precision instrumentation and high-frequency engineering work happening there is unusual, and it creates the kind of environment where people in adjacent specialisations actually talk to each other rather than operating in separate silos. That kind of cross-pollination is something I value and have not experienced enough of in my own career so far.

My background is in wireless communication signal processing. I completed my MSc in Electrical Engineering at Bukak National University in 2015 and have worked at Sumuvire Wireless since, first on modem receiver signal chains and more recently on channel characterisation. The work has been consistently close to hardware -- designing filter architectures, validating algorithms against measured channel data, dealing with the persistent gap between what a simulation predicts and what a physical propagation environment actually does.

The part of my experience I think is most relevant to what Kaikuvaara does is the measurement work. In 2021 and 2022 I ran a millimetre-wave channel sounding campaign that required setting up and calibrating RF measurement rigs at multiple sites, operating spectrum analysers and custom antenna configurations at 28 and 39 GHz, and then making sense of propagation data that did not always match the models. That kind of careful measurement discipline, where the calibration setup matters as much as the data it produces, is something I have come to value deeply and want to keep at the centre of my work going forward.

I also have working familiarity with Kalman filtering and estimation theory methods, which I see as increasingly relevant in sensor tracking and state estimation domains beyond wireless communications.

I took a year off between mid-2018 and late 2019 to travel. It was a planned break after two intensive years, and I returned sharper rather than rusty. The measurement campaign I ran afterward was the most technically demanding work I have done at Sumuvire.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the emphasis on measurement integrity in your instrumentation products. From what I have seen of your published specifications and product literature, the signal quality challenges you face are demanding in ways that feel familiar from my own measurement campaigns, even if the application domain is quite different. The idea of working somewhere that the precision of the measurement is the product itself, rather than just a step toward a specification number, is genuinely appealing.

I recognise my experience is narrower than what you probably need, and there are areas where I would have to learn. But measurement discipline and signal processing fundamentals transfer well, and I think there is value in bringing a perspective from a different corner of the RF world.

Happy to discuss further.

Kenji Sharma

application.cover_letter_markdown:
To the Hiring Manager,

I have spent the better part of two decades in wireless signal processing at Sumuvire Wireless, and there are things about that work I still find genuinely interesting. But I have reached a point where I want the systems I contribute to to end up somewhere other than a base station or a handset. Kaikuvaara's focus on remote-sensing instrumentation is what caught my attention. The engineering constraints in mission-critical instrument design -- reliability budgets, calibration regimes, the basic fact that nobody can go out and reboot the hardware if something drifts -- are fundamentally different from consumer wireless, and that difference is the attraction.

In the last three years at Sumuvire I have been working specifically on phased-array beamforming algorithms for 5G NR massive MIMO base stations. The core of that project involved designing digital beamforming weight computations for a 64-element planar array, simulating beam patterns under various steering and interference conditions, and validating the beam steering performance against over-the-air measurements in Sumuvire's anechoic chamber. It taught me a great deal about the practical interaction between array geometry, mutual coupling, and real-world beam pattern degradation -- problems that, from what I can tell from your published product specifications, are directly relevant to the sensor arrays Kaikuvaara builds.

Beyond the beamforming work, I also have familiarity with satellite and airborne platform requirements, which is part of what makes Kaikuvaara's remote-sensing focus appealing to me.

The long tenure at a single company could look like inertia, so I want to address that directly. Sumuvire went through enough technology generations during my time -- from early LTE to 5G millimetre-wave -- that staying meant continuously learning new things rather than coasting on existing knowledge. The underlying signal processing moved from single-carrier equalisation to massive spatial multiplexing, and my role evolved with it. What I have not had is the systems-engineering perspective that comes from working on a platform where signal processing is one component inside something larger and more constrained. That is a significant part of what I am looking for now.

My training at Gotaalv was in electrical engineering with an emphasis on statistical signal processing. The programme was taught entirely in English, and English has been my day-to-day working language at Sumuvire for the past seventeen years -- documentation, customer presentations, specification reviews, everything.

I am realistic about the gap between wireless communications and remote-sensing instrumentation. There is domain knowledge I would need to build. But the mathematical foundations overlap substantially -- array processing, spectral estimation, statistical signal processing -- and the engineering discipline of validating algorithm performance against physical measurements rather than simulations alone carries over directly. That is where I think I can contribute.

I would be glad to discuss what a transition like this might look like in practical terms.

Santiago Kim

application.cover_letter_markdown:
To the hiring team at Kaikuvaara Oy,

I am writing about the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role. My background is not a straight-line match -- I trained as a biomedical engineer and came into optical signal processing from the medical imaging side -- but the technical overlap turned out to be larger than I expected when I made the switch, and I think there are things in my profile worth considering.

At Sinikaari Optics I have spent the last five years working on sensor signal conditioning for industrial optical systems. The core of the work is making sure that the raw sensor output is clean, stable, and characterised well enough for downstream processing to trust it. That means noise floor analysis, drift compensation, and systematic validation against known reference standards. It is not glamorous, but it is the kind of work that directly determines whether a product performs in the field.

The project I am most satisfied with from my time at Sinikaari is the sensor commissioning I did in Oulu in 2023. I spent a month on-site at a paper mill getting a measurement system to work in a real industrial environment -- vibration, temperature swings, electrical interference from nearby machinery -- and the discipline of making a sensor system reliable under those conditions taught me things that lab work does not.

I also have some familiarity with satellite and airborne platform requirements from broader industry context.

The reason I am applying to Kaikuvaara specifically is that your instrumentation products operate in a domain where signal quality is not a nice-to-have but the entire point of the product. My experience centres on making sure the signal you measure is the signal that is actually there, and I believe that transfers across sensing modalities even when the specific technology differs.

I am currently based in the Netherlands but I have spent time working in Oulu and I am actively looking at relocating to Finland. I have EU citizenship and no logistical obstacles to a move.

I am realistic about the gaps in my profile relative to what you need, but I wanted to put my name forward.

Kristina Horvath

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Kaikuvaara Oy
Regarding: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

I realise this application probably looks unusual. I have spent my career in industrial equipment sales, not engineering, and I am aware that the technical requirements of this role go well beyond what my CV demonstrates. But I have been thinking about a career change for some time and I wanted to explain why I am writing to you specifically.

Over twenty-five years at Laitekallio I have become deeply familiar with the industrial equipment that manufacturers rely on, including various categories of sensing and measurement instrumentation. I have not designed these systems, but I have sold them, sat alongside customer engineering teams during installation, and been the first phone call when something does not perform as the datasheet promised. That has given me a particular understanding of this equipment -- not the designer's understanding, but the understanding of someone who has seen dozens of installations across different factory environments and knows what goes wrong and why.

The equipment side of my work has always been the part that interests me most. When I am on a customer site helping to commission a new system and we are working through a calibration issue together, that is when the job feels worthwhile. The quota targets and pipeline management that make up most of my actual responsibilities are things I can do well but they are not what gets me out of bed.

I took a year off in 2010 to travel and came back more aware than before that I wanted to move toward something technical. That did not happen at the time, partly because the practical barriers to switching careers at forty are real and partly because the income in technical sales is hard to walk away from. I have reached a point now where the question has shifted from whether I can afford to change to whether I can afford to keep not changing.

Kaikuvaara caught my attention because your instruments are exactly the kind of precision measurement technology I have spent my career around, from the other side of the table. I do not pretend to have the signal processing expertise the role requires. What I do have is over two decades of context about how measurement instruments get used in practice, what their operators actually need, and what the gap looks like between a product specification and a working installation. Whether that kind of knowledge has value to an engineering team is your call to make, not mine.

I would be happy to have a straightforward conversation about what I can and cannot bring to a role like this.

Sami Jarvinen
